# Dying Light 2: Stay Human

### "Humanity is dying. At least the parkour is alive."

**Recommended. Absolutely worth the fall.**

The world ended, civilization collapsed, and humanity somehow decided that living on rooftops was a reasonable career choice.

Welcome to Villedor.

Dying Light 2 takes everything that made the first game fun and throws you into a massive open world where every rooftop is a playground, every building is a shortcut, and every wrong turn can become a one-way trip to the ground floor.

The parkour feels incredible. Gliding across rooftops, swinging between buildings, and barely surviving a fall you definitely should not have survived never gets old. Combat is brutal, weapons break, infected swarm the streets, and sometimes the best strategy is to run like you've got 47 unpaid bills chasing you.

And then there's nighttime.

The streets become a death sentence, infected become nightmares with legs, and suddenly that tiny UV light looks more valuable than your entire inventory. You can spend the whole day feeling like an unstoppable badass, only to spend the night screaming internally while running for your life.

The story has its ups and downs, and not every choice hits as hard as it should. But the atmosphere, exploration, movement, and sheer chaos of surviving in Villedor make it ridiculously easy to lose hours in this world.

Is it perfect? No.

Does it always reach the same level of horror as the first game? Not quite.

But when you're flying off a skyscraper, deploying your paraglider at the last possible second, landing on a rooftop, and immediately dropkicking an infected into the next dimension, you remember exactly why you bought this game.

**Dying Light 2 isn't just about staying human. It's about losing 30 minutes of your life because you saw a cool rooftop and forgot you had actual missions to complete.**

**9/10 — The world may be falling apart, but I'm still hitting every rooftop like I own the place.**

*Keep moving. Trust nobody. And for the love of God, get inside before sunset.*

ONLY GET ON SALE, and be prepared for occasional bullshit for 1st playthrough if solo. It's hard to recommend this to anyone expecting the DL1 experience. This is more akin to FarCry where you need to focus quests and monuments for most of your xp (or night-grind), and grind "trophies" to make your items more usable.

Things like the awfully-slow climb animations and the un-upgraded parachute deploy being multiple seconds effectively stun lock you. Why does every enemy have a grab stun-lock animation that can trigger a mili-second before a melee is gonna dome them... Even the merc's homing knifes hitstun you. Had volatiles stun-lock me to death with spam b/c they always cancel ur melee swing early. Some of these problems only get solved at late-game (late-skills, booster-spam, tank-build, etc), and make the middle part on new characters annoying.

A lot of things weirdly prioritize the enemies over you, like how volatile attacks and leaps still hit you when they miss (leap is bounding-box with no LOS-check). Any zombie can grab u when ur melee is 1 frame from hitting them; One Volatile grabbed/pinned me through the middle of a solid wall lol?!?

I appreciate them giving out the poorly received DLC in order to breed good will for The Beast, and after playing some of that I'm glad they took some advice here like condensing skill tree to make sure certain skills are there earlier. The parkour here can feel great when it knows to be split into smaller bursts and not in ones where you die at the end of chain section because a 5 fps dip can skip your input for some reason at the end...

The graphics are great and seems more optimized than The Beast atm... Story is ok and the ending/villain is meh, but there are things about it that can be enjoyable. If they could ever rebalance some of these factors (like skill-tree condensing), it could make a more smooth experience. The Beast took some of this advice so I know it's possible for DL2 to improve as such. The endgame movement feels great, so it feels awful when ur paraglider and grapple arent upgraded on new saves.

The Review

Dying Light 2 is one of those games that took me a while to fully appreciate. The story and characters can be hit or miss, and some of the dialogue feels a little cheesy, but once you get into the parkour and combat, the game becomes seriously fun.

The parkour is easily the best part. Running across rooftops, jumping between buildings, and escaping a horde of infected never really gets old. The nighttime sections are also genuinely tense, especially when you’re underleveled and suddenly realize you’ve got way more zombies chasing you than you can handle.

The combat feels good once you unlock more skills and get better gear, and there’s a decent amount of freedom in how you approach situations. The world itself is also fun to explore, with plenty of random encounters, side activities, and things to discover.

The Reloaded Edition is a great package if you’re starting fresh, especially with the extra content and improvements that have been added since launch. That said, the game still has some bugs and occasional jank, and the story definitely isn't going to be the main reason you keep playing.

Overall, it's a really fun open-world zombie game with fantastic movement, satisfying combat, and a surprisingly addictive gameplay loop.

8/10 — If you like zombies, parkour, and exploring open worlds, definitely worth picking up.

Very mediocre game, my amount of hours are just from trying to 100% the game out of a principal of 100%ing dying light games since I liked the first game. This game has more content than dying light 1 and is somehow just less fun to play. The map is very samey looking uninteresting and boring to explore, the story granted is better than the first game by a long shot but is still not very interesting, they introduce characters and u barely get to know them and ur just supposed to care about them when they die (cough cough lawan). They try harded so much to have a good story almost every side quest with an npc you see literally one time in the entire game having like 5 minutes of dialogue to wait for, once i realised there is no achievement for finishing every side quest i completely stopped doing them. The night times are what this series is best known for, literally being the slogan of the game, and the night times in this game are way less scary than the first game. First off its not nearly as dark so the atmosphere is already way less scary and volatiles in this game just overall arent very intimidating, I found myself getting more angry dealing with them than scared, since they completely make you unable to move your screen when hitting you and they just sometimes decide to completely ignore the uv light and molly whop you 3 times and youre just dead.

The parkour is frustratingly buggy and jank sometimes and I encountered a ton of bugs sometimes getting me killed and making me lose legend points and time, the dropkick is also just so fucking weird and jank to use why the hell do you float like youre on the moon and why does it just maintain your upward momentum when you do it, this has also made me fall to my death multiple times and it just made me not want to use it most of the time, this was the most iconic attack from the first game and they basically shat on it. The combat at first was way less satisfying than the first game and I still think it is, but it mostly grew on me the longer I played. Every single quarantine is the exact same and its so boring and uninteresting to do especially since every quarantine zone in the first game was completely different which always gave you a new experience. Volatile "nests" are also just laughably garbage compared to the first game aswell, in dying light 1 the nests were huge with a ton of zombies and body piles and gore everywhere and really blood gorey etc, in this game its just a random fucking volatile half way in the ground with like 2 of them protecting it in some random building... fucking pathetic. The guns in this game are way too overpowered, basically the only downside is attracting virals which doesnt even matter 90% of the time. In the lore its talked about how ammo is super rare and scarce but you can buy it infinitely and even find it on zombies? really dont understand that lol. The grappling hook was eviscerated in this game, I can admit it was super overpowered in the first game, parkour basically became redundant once you got it, but in this game it just turned into a fucking tarzan rope swing which you almost never use, besides main story locations giving you the perfect areas to use it, or just using a tech to scale a building with no parkour which makes the nerf basically pointless. Every gre anomaly is just the exact same with more health dependent on the tier, more laziness. The dlc is also mostly uninteresting, it makes it sound like its some gladiator arena dlc where u constantly fight people but its not, you fight people maybe like... once or twice, then youre just completing mostly unfun challenges though to be fair some of them were pretty cool, until you get the rank behind the final boss then youre actually put into the arena, and surprise surprise the final boss is a complete pushover, the store page rating of it is accurate. 

OK the last thing I wanna talk about is the achievements. Most of them are fine but holy shit there are some that are just so braindead that I do not understand how a developer decided to keep it as is. The save 50 people achievement is cancer, theres about 6 different variations of the blue diamond marker and I believe only 2 of them count towards the achievement, If you get unlucky and its not one of those 2 have fun wandering around for about 5 minutes testing your luck again about 50 times, afaik there is no way to manipulate the odds in this game unlike the first one. Every single collectible achievement besides the graffiti are utter bullshit, there are some you literally cannot get anymore if you progress too far without completing a random side quest, unless youre just following a guide prior youre fucked unless you wanna replay the game 2-3 times. The 1 million money achievement is also really stupid, as it takes so ungodly long unless you manipulate it with a dupe glitch or abuse a loophole of selling and re buying without leaving the menu (this is what I did), and the 900km achievement is the epitome of fucking bullshit, whatever dev decided to keep this in the game I hope you rot in hell for doing this, I replayed the entire game twice and left the achievement for last and i was not even half way, the achievement requirement is 22X THE AMOUNT OF DISTANCE COMPARED TO THE FIRST GAME, GO FUCK YOURSELF. Over 100 hours and I just decided to sam the achievement, I am not doing this legit.

Overall very mid game that is mostly just worse than the first game, but I think it is still worth playing if youre a fan of the series, I would rate this game as a neutral rating, but that does not exist so I will be voting it as not recommended. If you decide to 100% this game, GOOD NIGHT AND GOOD LUCK
